decisions.rationale: Whimsicott plus Gholdengo gives immediate Prankster Tailwind and powerful spread pressure, with Protect available to scout Mega Metagross or opposing speed control. Milotic punishes Gyarados's Intimidate and checks Fire/Ground threats, while Arcanine adds Intimidate, Heat Wave pressure, and burns into the opponent's physical-heavy roster.
decisions.notebook: Core plan remains Whimsicott/Gholdengo for immediate Tailwind plus spread offense. Milotic is the preferred Intimidate-punishing bring against Gyarados and can provide Icy Wind or Recover. Arcanine is valuable into Steel/Flying targets and physical attackers through Heat Wave, Snarl, Will-O-Wisp, and Intimidate. Sinistcha is the alternative defensive bring when redirection, Strength Sap, or Hospitality is more important; Grimmsnarl is the screen/Parting Shot option for slower attrition games.

decisions.rationale: Lead Metagross+Gyarados: Mega Meta at 178 Spe outspeedes Gholdengo/Arcanine/etc, EQ hits Gholdengo 2x SE while Gyarados Flying-immune. Gyarados Intimidate+Lum Berry handles Prankster status, Taunt pressures non-priority setters, Waterfall/Crunch hit Arcanine/Sinistcha SE. Back Snorlax (Ghost-immune Gholdengo wall, Thick Fat for Arcanine) + Corviknight (Tailwind speed control, Mirror Armor reflects Intimidate).
decisions.notebook: Game 1 lead plan: Metagross+Gyarados lead, Snorlax+Corviknight back. Mega Metagross EQ is the primary Gholdengo answer (2x SE, Gyarados immune via Flying). Gyarados Lum Berry absorbs one Prankster status. Snorlax is the Ghost-immune special wall for Gholdengo Shadow Ball and Thick Fat covers Arcanine. Corviknight provides Tailwind speed control from back; Mirror Armor reflects opponent Intimidate (Arcanine). Key speed benchmarks: Mega Meta 178 Spe ties/outspeeds most of their team except Whimsicott (149-184). If opponent sets Tailwind first via Prankster Whimsicott, consider switching to Corviknight for mirror Tailwind or playing slow with Snorlax. Watch for Sinistcha Rage Powder redirecting single-target moves; spread moves (EQ, Make It Rain) bypass it. Strength Sap drops Mega Meta Atk (Tough Claws replaces Clear Body post-Mega). Competitive Milotic punishes Intimidate — avoid double Intimidate into Milotic unless Snorlax/Toxapex available to wall it.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott’s priority Tailwind acts before all ordinary foe moves, ensuring Gholdengo outspeeds afterward. Gholdengo’s Shadow Ball is guaranteed to OHKO Metagross, removing the strongest immediate threat while preserving both active Pokémon and establishing the speed advantage.
decisions.notebook: Whimsicott/Gholdengo remains the preferred immediate lead for priority Tailwind into strong spread or single-target special offense. Milotic is the preferred follow-up into Gyarados and opposing Intimidate cycles; Arcanine is valuable against Steel/Flying and physical attackers. Preserve Milotic for Icy Wind or Recover when speed control or longevity is needed.

decisions.rationale: Protect+Mega on Metagross is safest: Prankster Tailwind lets Gholdengo outspeed Mega Meta (208-272 vs 143-178) and Shadow Ball can OHKO (59.9-157.4%). Protect guarantees safe Mega Evo while Gyarados Crunch chunks Gholdengo for 35-78%, setting up a KO next turn. Gyarados survives any Gholdengo hit (Shadow Ball only 29.7-78.2%).
decisions.notebook: Game 1 lead: Meta+Gyara front, Snorlax+Corvi back. Key damage benchmarks: Gholdengo Shadow Ball on Mega Meta 59.9-157.4% (possible OHKO via Life Orb Modest). Focus Blast NEUTRAL on Metagross (Fighting 2x Steel × 0.5x Psychic = 1x). Mega Meta EQ (spread) on Gholdengo 29.9-79%. Gyarados Crunch on Gholdengo 35.1-77.8%. Combined EQ+Crunch ~65-157% (likely KO if both connect). Shadow Ball on Gyarados 29.7-78.2% (no OHKO). Prankster Tailwind (+1 pri) resolves before normal moves but after Protect (+4). With Tailwind, Gholdengo outspeeds Mega Meta. Plan: T1 Protect+Mega to safely evolve, chip Gholdengo with Crunch. T2: finish Gholdengo with EQ or bring Corviknight for Tailwind mirror if opponent speed control persists. Watch for Sinistcha Strength Sap on Mega Meta (Tough Claws replaces Clear Body post-Mega, no stat-drop immunity). Competitive Milotic punishes Intimidate—avoid double Intimidate into it.

decisions.rationale: Encore Metagross-Mega’s previously used Protect, preventing its immediate offensive pressure, while Gholdengo Protects to block Gyarados’s likely super-effective Crunch and preserve the 40% HP attacker. This creates a safe turn to attack next turn under Tailwind.
decisions.notebook: Whimsicott/Gholdengo remains the preferred lead. Preserve Tailwind turns and use Whimsicott’s priority disruption to constrain opposing Protect or setup patterns. Milotic remains the preferred Gyarados and Intimidate-cycle follow-up; Arcanine is valuable against Steel/Flying and physical attackers. Preserve Milotic for Icy Wind or Recover when speed control or longevity is needed.

decisions.rationale: Switching Meta→Corviknight dodges Prankster Encore that would lock Meta into Protect (last move). Corviknight brings Tailwind for speed parity and resists Make It Rain (0.25x). Gyarados Crunches Gholdengo at 39%: if Gholdengo attacks, Life Orb recoil drops it to ~29%, making Crunch (35.1% min) a guaranteed KO. If Gholdengo Protects, Crunch fails but Corviknight enters safely. Worst case double-target on Gyarados (46-123% combined) risks a trade, but Gholdengo still falls to Crunch after LO recoil.
decisions.notebook: Damage benchmarks verified: Crunch on Gholdengo 35.1-77.8% (not guaranteed KO at 39% without LO recoil; guaranteed if Gholdengo attacks first, dropping to ~29%). EQ spread on Gholdengo 34-75.3% (not guaranteed alone). Combined EQ+Crunch 69.1% min = guaranteed KO if both connect. Shadow Ball on Corviknight 32.2-87.9% (survives). Shadow Ball on Gyarados 29.7-78.2%. Moonblast on Gyarados 16.3-44.7%. Combined double-target on Gyarados 46-123% (possible KO). Prankster Encore (+1 pri) outspeeds all my non-Protect moves; switching out is the only Encore dodge (fails on incoming mon with no move history). Plan: T2 switch Meta→Corvi to dodge Encore + Crunch Gholdengo. T3 Corviknight Tailwind for speed parity, Gyarados continues pressure. Avoid double Intimidate into Competitive Milotic. Watch Sinistcha Strength Sap on physical attackers.

decisions.rationale: Encore Gyarados’s revealed Crunch, constraining its options while preserving Whimsicott’s priority disruption. Switch Gholdengo to Milotic to avoid another likely super-effective Crunch KO, retain Gholdengo for later, and establish the preferred Gyarados check; Whimsicott’s Focus Sash preserves it through Brave Bird.

Corviknight sets Tailwind for speed parity against opponent's 2-turn Tailwind. Gyarados Crunches Gholdengo at 39%: if it attacks first, LO recoil drops it to ~29% and Crunch (35.1% min) KOs. If Gholdengo Protects (reduced rate), Crunch whiffs but Tailwind is up for next turn. Encore risk on Gyarados is acceptable—locked Crunch is still useful and switching breaks it. Make It Rain only does 18-32% to Corviknight (resisted+spread).
decisions.notebook: Damage benchmarks: Crunch on Gholdengo 35.1-77.8% (KO at 39% if LO recoil drops it first). Make It Rain spread on Corviknight 17.8-31.5%. Gyarados Speed 127, with Tailwind 254—may not outspeed Gholdengo (208-272 w/ TW). Whimsicott Focus Sash means it survives one hit at 1 HP. Encore locks for 3 turns; switching breaks it. Prankster Encore (+1 pri) outspeeds all non-Protect moves. Avoid double Intimidate into Competitive Milotic. Watch Sinistcha Strength Sap on physical attackers. Gyarados Lum Berry still intact. Opponent Tailwind has 2 turns left after T3.

decisions.rationale: Priority Encore locks Corviknight into its revealed Tailwind, denying Brave Bird and other pressure while constraining its switch-or-waste options. Milotic uses Icy Wind for spread Speed control against both foes; this helps offset their Tailwind and supports the next turn after our Tailwind expires.
decisions.notebook: Whimsicott/Gholdengo remains the preferred lead. Use Whimsicott’s Prankster Encore and Taunt to constrain opposing Tailwind, Protect, and setup patterns. Milotic is the preferred Gyarados answer and can leverage Competitive after Intimidate; preserve it for Icy Wind speed control or Recover. Arcanine is valuable into Steel/Flying and physical attackers. Track revealed opposing sets: Mega Metagross has Meteor Mash, Earthquake, Bullet Punch, Protect; Gyarados has Waterfall, Crunch, Taunt, Protect and Intimidate; Corviknight has Brave Bird, Tailwind, U-turn, Protect and Mirror Armor.

decisions.rationale: Brave Bird SE on Whimsicott breaks Focus Sash (leaves at 1HP or very low—any hit KOs next turn). Crunch chips Milotic to ~22-49% while Gyarados resists Muddy Water (0.5x). Corviknight takes 41-61% from +2 Muddy Water but survives. Next turn opponent TW expires; Gyarados at 254 outspeeds all foes and KOs Whimsicott. If Corviknight gets Encored into Tailwind, switch it out to break. Metagross preserved in back for safe entry later.
decisions.notebook:
Damage benchmarks: Brave Bird on Whimsicott 69.5-164.4% (breaks sash or leaves very low, any hit KOs next turn). U-turn only 11.4-27.4%—does NOT break Focus Sash, useless for sash breaking. +2 Milotic Muddy Water spread: Corviknight 41.1-60.9%, Metagross-Mega 30.5-83.2% (wide range—risky switch-in), Gyarados resisted 0.5x. Gyarados Crunch on -1 Def Milotic 31.2-57.6% (20% def drop re-procs Competitive to +4 SpA).
Focus Sash only works at full HP; any prior damage disables it.
Encore: applied T3, lasts T3-T5. Switching breaks it. Prankster Encore (+1 pri) beats non-Protect moves. If Corviknight uses a move, Whimsicott can Encore into Tailwind (last move T3). Protect (+4 pri) goes first but Encore then locks into Protect (bad). Switching Corviknight out breaks Encore.
Speed: After opponent TW expires, Gyarados 254 outspeeds all foes (Whimsicott 149-184, Milotic 101-133, Gholdengo 104-136, Arcanine 126-161, Sinistcha 90-122, Grimmsnarl 80-112). Metagross 356 with TW outspeeds everything.
Plan: KO Whimsicott T5, pressure Milotic, bring Metagross in safely later. Gholdengo at 39%—one hit KOs. Watch Arcanine Intimidate, Sinistcha Strength Sap/Rage Powder, Grimmsnarl screens. Gyarados Lum Berry intact.

decisions.rationale: Set Tailwind with Prankster while Milotic Protects through Gyarados’s Encore-locked Crunch. This preserves Milotic at 45%, lets opposing Tailwind expire sooner, and positions both Pokémon to regain speed control next turn.
decisions.notebook: Continue preferring Whimsicott/Gholdengo lead. Preserve Milotic as the primary Gyarados answer and speed-control resource; Competitive has activated twice from reflected Intimidate drops. Arcanine remains valuable into Mega Metagross and Corviknight. Opposing revealed sets remain: Mega Metagross Meteor Mash/Earthquake/Bullet Punch/Protect; Gyarados Waterfall/Crunch/Taunt/Protect; Corviknight Brave Bird/Tailwind/U-turn/Protect with Mirror Armor.

decisions.rationale: Switch Corviknight to Snorlax to break Encore and bring a safe +4 Muddy Water sponge (22.5-68%, survives). Gyarados is Encored into Crunch—target Whimsicott to break Focus Sash (1 HP). Next turn Gyarados is free from Encore, outspeeds all foes under Tailwind, and KOs Whimsicott with any hit. Avoids risking Metagross to +4 Muddy Water (50-139% range, possible OHKO).

Gyarados Crunch on -1 Def Milotic: base 13.9-45.9% ×1.5 for Def drop = 20.85-68.85%—possible KO from 51% but not guaranteed; 20% Def drop re-procs Competitive to +6. Metagross 356 with TW outspeeds everything. Plan: KO Whimsicott T5, pressure Milotic, bring Metagross in safely later. Gholdengo at 39%—one hit KOs. Watch Arcanine Intimidate, Sinistcha Strength Sap/Rage Powder, Grimmsnarl screens. Gyarados Lum Berry intact.

decisions.rationale: Encore locks Gyarados into its revealed Crunch, preventing Taunt or Protect while Whimsicott acts first. Milotic should use boosted spread Muddy Water to pressure both foes; it can substantially damage Snorlax and may secure accuracy drops, while preserving recovery for a later turn.
decisions.notebook: Continue prioritizing Whimsicott/Gholdengo leads. Milotic is the primary Gyarados answer and valuable speed-control resource; Competitive has activated twice from reflected Intimidate drops. Arcanine remains important against Mega Metagross and Corviknight. Revealed opposing sets: Mega Metagross Meteor Mash/Earthquake/Bullet Punch/Protect; Gyarados Waterfall/Crunch/Taunt/Protect; Corviknight Brave Bird/Tailwind/U-turn/Protect with Mirror Armor.

decisions.rationale: Keep Whimsicott active to exploit Tailwind and pressure the weakened Gyarados while its Encore lock persists. Switch Milotic to Arcanine rather than exposing Gholdengo to a likely Dark attack; Arcanine also provides Intimidate and remains valuable against Mega Metagross and Corviknight.
decisions.notebook: Whimsicott/Gholdengo remains the preferred lead combination. Milotic is the primary Gyarados answer and a valuable speed-control resource when available; Competitive can punish reflected Intimidate drops. Arcanine is important for checking Mega Metagross and Corviknight. Opposing revealed sets: Mega Metagross has Meteor Mash, Earthquake, Bullet Punch, Protect; Gyarados has Waterfall, Crunch, Taunt, Protect; Corviknight has Brave Bird, Tailwind, U-turn, Protect, with Mirror Armor.

decisions.rationale: Double into Milotic: Earthquake (24.3-55.3%) + Crunch (28.2-64.1%) = 52.5% min > 51% HP, should KO. EQ also chips Whimsicott 9-21.5%. Gyarados immune to EQ (Flying). Both survive +4 Muddy Water (Snorlax 31-57%, Gyarados 27-49%). Milotic Protect rate reduced. Must remove +4 Milotic before my Tailwind expires this turn.
decisions.notebook: Damage benchmarks: Snorlax EQ on Milotic 24.3-55.3% (spread, 1x). Gyarados Crunch on Milotic 28.2-64.1% (Def -1). Combined min 52.5% > 51% = KO. EQ chips Whimsicott 9-21.5%. +4 Muddy Water: Snorlax 31-57%, Gyarados 27-49% (resisted). Fire Punch on Whimsicott 38.3-87.4% (2x SE). After my TW expires T6, opponent TW remains 2 turns—foe outspeeds everything. Plan: KO Milotic T6, then clean up Whimsicott (low HP) and remaining foes. Metagross 178/356 with TW outspeeds all; bring in safely after TW drops. Gyarados Lum Berry intact. Watch Encore locks, Arcanine Intimidate on switch-in.

decisions.rationale: Encore Snorlax into its revealed Earthquake, preventing Protect and other options while making its spread damage manageable. Arcanine Protects to avoid the super-effective Earthquake; Gyarados remains forced to Crunch Whimsicott, preserving both Pokémon and the Tailwind advantage for the next turn.
decisions.notebook: Whimsicott/Gholdengo remains the preferred lead combination. Milotic is the primary Gyarados answer and a valuable speed-control resource when available; Competitive can punish reflected Intimidate drops. Arcanine is important for checking Mega Metagross and Corviknight. Gyarados is Encore-prone and has revealed Waterfall, Crunch, Taunt, and Protect; Mega Metagross has Meteor Mash, Earthquake, Bullet Punch, and Protect; Corviknight has Brave Bird, Tailwind, U-turn, Protect, and Mirror Armor. Preserve Arcanine against Metagross and Corviknight when practical.

decisions.rationale: Gyarados is Encore-locked at 30% with -1 Atk/Acc/Spe—must switch. Metagross at 100% is best incoming. Snorlax Fire Punch chunks Whimsicott 27.5-53.3% (SE), setting up Metagross Meteor Mash KO next turn (97-217.8%, possible OHKO from full). Protect risks Encore lock into Protect; Earthquake hits incoming Metagross SE. Opponent TW has 1 turn left after this; Metagross can clean up.
decisions.notebook: Damage benchmarks: Metagross-Mega Meteor Mash on Whimsicott 97-217.8% (Tough Claws, SE Fairy, possible OHKO from full). Metagross EQ on Arcanine 36.5-80% spread. Arcanine Heat Wave on Metagross 38.5-86.5% (Charcoal, spread, SE Steel). Snorlax Fire Punch on Whimsicott 27.5-53.3% at -1 Atk. Arcanine Heat Wave on Snorlax 15.1-22.4% (Charcoal, spread). Plan: switch out Encore-locked Gyarados to break lock, bring Metagross, chip Whimsicott with Fire Punch, KO with Meteor Mash next turn. Opponent TW expires after T8. Metagross 178 Spe outspeeds Gholdengo (104-136) and Arcanine (126-161) without TW, but may lose speed tie to Whimsicott (149-184). Gyarados Lum Berry intact. Corviknight 76% with Mirror Armor, can set Tailwind if needed. Watch for Arcanine Will-O-Wisp on Metagross (burn halves Atk). Snorlax at 50% with Leftovers recovery.

decisions.rationale: Encore Metagross to its previously revealed Protect, limiting its immediate options while Arcanine uses its fastest, super-effective spread attack. Heat Wave has a possible KO on Metagross and pressures both foes; preserving Arcanine is important against Metagross and Corviknight.
decisions.notebook: Whimsicott/Gholdengo remains the preferred lead combination. Milotic is the primary Gyarados answer and Competitive can punish reflected Intimidate drops when Milotic is available. Preserve Arcanine against Mega Metagross and Corviknight when practical. Gyarados has revealed Waterfall, Crunch, Taunt, and Protect and is Encore-prone. Mega Metagross has revealed Meteor Mash, Earthquake, Bullet Punch, and Protect. Corviknight has revealed Brave Bird, Tailwind, U-turn, Protect, and Mirror Armor.

decisions.rationale: Metagross Protect (+4 priority) guaranteed before Whimsicott Encore (+1), keeping Metagross free and avoiding 21-26% ally Earthquake chip. Snorlax EQ chips Arcanine 22-50% (2x SE). Switching to Gyarados risks Moonblast KO (55%) or opponent Taunt. T9 Tailwind expires, opening Bullet Punch speed gamble vs Encore.
decisions.notebook: Metagross-Mega: 178 Spe, Atk 185, Tough Claws. Bullet Punch on Whimsicott 50% HP: 44.3-103.7% (possible KO, ~90% if it outspeeds). Meteor Mash on Whimsicott: 97-217.8% (guaranteed KO). Snorlax EQ at -1 Atk on Arcanine: 22-50% spread; on Metagross: 21-26% ally. Protect +4 always beats Prankster Encore +1. Whimsicott raw Spe 149-184 (Timid) — likely maxed at 184, meaning Metagross 178 probably loses speed tie for +1 priority moves without Tailwind. Gyarados at 30% with Lum Berry: Moonblast KO risk 55%, Snarl/Heat Wave safe. Corviknight immune to Ground (Flying). Plan T9: switch Snorlax out (break Encore), Metagross Bullet Punch on Whimsicott if speed favorable, else Protect again (1/3 success). Opponent Encore pattern: every turn T4-T7. Gholdengo 39% LO, outspeeds nothing on my team without TW. Arcanine Protect used T7, reduced success T8.

decisions.rationale: Moonblast pressures Snorlax while Metagross remains locked into its repeated Protect. Arcanine Protects to avoid Snorlax's Encored Earthquake, preserving it as a key answer to Mega Metagross and Corviknight.
decisions.notebook: Mega Metagross has revealed Meteor Mash, Earthquake, Bullet Punch, and Protect; it is Encore-prone. Snorlax has revealed Body Slam, Earthquake, Fire Punch, and Protect and is currently Encore-locked. Gyarados has revealed Waterfall, Crunch, Taunt, and Protect and is Encore-prone. Milotic is unavailable this game; preserve Arcanine when practical and retain Gholdengo as the preferred replacement for Whimsicott.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Switch Snorlax to Corviknight to break Encore and bring in a healthy utility mon. Metagross Bullet Punch on Whimsicott: guaranteed KO (44.3% min dmg > 41% HP) if it lands. Speed contest vs Prankster Encore is ~50/50 but far better EV than Protect (33% success) or Meteor Mash (Encore always first, locks into Protect). If BP KOs Whimsicott, opponent brings in Gholdengo 39% which Metagross outspeeds — strong position.
decisions.notebook: Metagross-Mega: 178 Spe, Atk 185, Tough Claws. Bullet Punch on Whimsicott 41% HP: 44.3-103.7% = guaranteed KO. Meteor Mash on Whimsicott: guaranteed KO but 0 priority loses to Prankster Encore (+1). compare_action_order does NOT account for Prankster — Bullet Punch vs Encore reported as guaranteed first but Meteor Mash vs Encore shows equal priority, confirming tool ignores Prankster. Real BP vs Encore is speed contest 178 vs 149-184. Snorlax EQ at -1 Atk on Arcanine: 22-50% spread; on Metagross: 21-26% ally. Protect +4 always beats Prankster Encore +1 but success rate 1/3 after consecutive use. Heat Wave spread on Metagross 78%: 32-106% (possible KO); on Corviknight 76%: 33-118% (possible KO, Steel weak to Fire); on Gyarados 30%: 7-26% (survives). Arcanine Timid support set (Heat Wave/Snarl/Wisp/Protect) with Charcoal — likely moderate SpA investment. Gyarados 30% Lum Berry, Intimidate not useful vs special attackers. Corviknight 76% Sharp Beak Mirror Armor — best long-term switch for Tailwind/U-turn utility. Gholdengo 39% LO Modest 104-136 Spe — outsped by Metagross 178, outspeeds Corviknight 87. Plan: KO Whimsicott to remove Encore threat, then pressure Gholdengo/Arcanine with Metagross speed advantage.

decisions.rationale: Shadow Ball guarantees the KO on Mega Metagross, while Heat Wave pressures both foes and can finish Corviknight. Metagross may move first with Earthquake, but the damage estimate leaves Gholdengo able to survive it; removing Metagross is the highest-value line.
decisions.notebook: Mega Metagross has revealed Meteor Mash, Earthquake, Bullet Punch, and Protect; it is Encore-prone and takes super-effective damage from Shadow Ball and Heat Wave. Snorlax has revealed Body Slam, Earthquake, Fire Punch, and Protect and is Encore-prone. Gyarados has revealed Waterfall, Crunch, Taunt, and Protect and is Encore-prone. Preserve Arcanine when practical; retain Gholdengo as the preferred replacement for Whimsicott.

decisions.rationale: Metagross EQ hits both foes 2x SE while Corviknight (Flying) is immune. EQ+Brave Bird guarantees Arcanine KO (67% min > 64% HP). EQ likely KOs Gholdengo at 39% HP. If both fall, instant win—opponent has no remaining Pokémon. Metagross unrevealed EQ = surprise factor. Even if Gholdengo Protects, we still remove Arcanine and face 1 foe with 3 Pokémon.
decisions.notebook: Metagross-Mega Jolly 178 Spe, 185 Atk, Tough Claws. EQ is non-contact so Tough Claws doesn't boost it. EQ spread vs Gholdengo 39%: 34-75.3% (likely KO). EQ spread vs Arcanine 64%: 36.5-83.6%. Corviknight Brave Bird vs Arcanine: 30.5-69.7%. EQ+BB min 67% > 64% = guaranteed Arcanine KO. Arcanine Heat Wave spread: 32-106% Metagross, 33-118% Corviknight (possible KO each). Gholdengo Shadow Ball LO: 50-157% Metagross (possible KO). Arcanine Protect used 2x = reduced rate. Gholdengo Protect used 1x = normal rate. Opponent brought 4: Whimsicott(fainted), Milotic(fainted), Gholdengo, Arcanine. KOing both active = instant win. Snorlax 53% Leftovers Thick Fat Adamant 50 Spe. Gyarados 30% Lum Berry Intimidate Adamant 127 Spe. Corviknight 76% Sharp Beak Mirror Armor Impish 87 Spe, 107 Atk. Tailwind expired both sides turn 8.

reflections.summary: Lost because the brought four lacked a safe answer to Mega Metagross's Earthquake: Arcanine and Gholdengo were both vulnerable, while Corviknight supplied Tailwind and a Ground immunity. The preview plan was poor for this matchup; retaining both Arcanine and Gholdengo exposed the team to one spread attack. No Mega Stone holder was shown, so there was no suitable Mega evolution to leverage.
reflections.adjustment: Change the four at preview by replacing Arcanine or Gholdengo with an available Ground-immune or Ground-resistant option, and preserve that protection for Mega Metagross. Do not rely on Encore as the primary answer when Metagross can Protect and then use Bullet Punch or Earthquake.
reflections.notebook: Mega Metagross's revealed set includes Meteor Mash, Earthquake, Bullet Punch, and Protect; it combines spread Ground pressure with priority and can stall Encore through Protect. Corviknight has revealed Tailwind and provides a Ground immunity, so plan for speed control plus Earthquake positioning. Avoid pairing Arcanine and Gholdengo as the main endgame into this core; prioritize a Ground-safe fourth and preserve Gholdengo only when Metagross's Earthquake is covered. Snorlax, Gyarados, and Mega Metagross remain vulnerable to Encore, but Protect timing makes Encore unreliable as the sole plan.

reflections.summary: Won by exploiting Metagross-Mega's Earthquake spread alongside Corviknight's Flying-type immunity to KO both remaining opponent Pokémon (Gholdengo and Arcanine) simultaneously on turn 10. Team preview was strong: Metagross-Mega's Steel/Ground coverage matched well into the opponent's Steel- and Fire-weak core, and Corviknight provided Tailwind speed control plus safe Earthquake immunity. Opponent's Whimsicott Encore locked Snorlax into Earthquake but ultimately couldn't prevent the sweep.
reflections.adjustment: Opponent may swap in Sinistcha (Rage Powder redirect) or Grimmsnarl (screens/Parting Shot) next game to better handle Metagross. Consider leading Metagross more aggressively and keep Bullet Punch for priority cleanup. If opponent brings Sinistcha, target it before committing to Earthquake spreads, as Rage Powder would redirect away from Gholdengo/Arcanine.
reflections.notebook: Opponent roster: Whimsicott (FocusSash, Prankster, Timid, Tailwind/Encore/Taunt/Moonblast), Gholdengo (LifeOrb, Modest, MakeItRain/ShadowBall/FocusBlast/Protect), Milotic (Leftovers, Competitive, Modest, MuddyWater/IcyWind/Recover/Protect), Arcanine (Charcoal, Intimidate, Timid, HeatWave/Snarl/WillOWisp/Protect), Sinistcha (SitrusBerry, Hospitality, Calm, RagePowder/MatchaGotcha/StrengthSap/Protect — not brought G1), Grimmsnarl (LightClay, Prankster, Careful, Reflect/LightScreen/PartingShot/SpiritBreak — not brought G1). Opponent uses Protect liberally (Arcanine 2x, Gholdengo 1x in 10 turns). Whimsicott Encore is a key disruption tool. Opponent favors speed control + spread damage. Metagross-Mega EQ spread KO'd Gholdengo 39% and Arcanine 64% simultaneously with Corviknight immune. Corviknight Mirror Armor reflects Intimidate. Plan G2: expect opponent to adjust bring toward Sinistcha or Grimmsnarl for Metagross answers; prepare for redirect/screens.
